source_note: Topic structure follows the Pearson Edexcel GCSE Psychology specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

connections.why: You choose an experimental design to manipulate the IV and measure the DV while controlling extraneous variables
Each research method produces particular kinds of qualitative or quantitative data
Quantitative data is summarised with descriptive statistics and graphs
The ethics taught in design feed directly into the ethical-issues debate
Peterson and Peterson used an experimental design like those taught in research methods
Piliavin's bystander study is a field observation of the kind covered in research methods
Piaget's cognitive stages map onto the maturation of the developing brain
Piaget and Inhelder's three-mountains task tests the egocentrism predicted by the theory
Both explain how learning and effort shape development, with contrasting emphases
The multi-store model formalises the encoding, storage and retrieval processes
Bartlett's War of the Ghosts is the study behind his reconstructive theory
Amnesia patterns reveal the separate STM and LTM stores of the multi-store model
Knowing each lobe's function lets you predict the effect of damaging it
Encoding and storing memories depends on synaptic transmission between neurons
Brain regions provide the physical basis for encoding and retrieving memories
Neurotransmitter and genetic explanations of depression draw on brain biology
CBT treats depression by targeting the faulty thinking the cognitive theory describes
Learning explanations of addiction motivate biological drug treatments as an alternative
Genetic versus learning explanations are the heart of the nature-nurture debate
Defining obedience and deindividuation sets up the study of obedience to authority
Piliavin's subway study tests the personal and situational factors in bystander intervention
Obedience and social learning both explain how others shape antisocial behaviour
Bandura's Bobo doll study is the evidence base for social learning theory of crime
Reducing reoffending weighs punishment against rehabilitative treatments
